judged_text: The DB fallback assigns the raw prisma.credential.findUnique result — fetched without the app relation, hence with no appName — into calendarCredential and hands it to getCalendar, which resolves the integration from credential.appName. getCalendar returns null for the appName-less credential, so calendar?.deleteEvent(...) is a silent no-op: cancelling the collective bookings this PR targets, whose reference credentialId belongs to a teammate or team rather than bookingToDelete.user, leaves the event live on that calendar with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the new fallback path for missing `calendarCredential` does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and assigns the raw result directly to `calendarCredential`, then calls `getCalendar(calendarCredential)` and later `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`. Elsewhere in this diff (e.g. `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` / `updateCalendarEvents`) when fetching a credential from DB, the code explicitly includes `app.slug` and constructs a `CredentialWithAppName` (`appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug`) before using calendar creation/update APIs, implying the calendar resolution depends on app metadata. The cancellation fallback does not fetch/build `appName`, so `getCalendar(...)` can fail to resolve the integration and return a falsy calendar, making `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` a silent no-op (and `apiDeletes.push(...)` pushes `undefined`). This would leave the external event undeleted with no surfaced error.
